english.title: Endanger another during sea crossing entering UK in breach of deportation order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly entered the United Kingdom by water from

(A)_[France]_
(B)_[Belgium]_
(C)_[the Netherlands]_

in breach of a deportation order made **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF ORDER..), and, during the relevant period, did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY ACT..), that caused, or created a risk of, the death of, or serious personal injury to, another person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 24(A1), (E1A) and (F1) of the Immigration Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
committed an offence under section 24(A1) of the Immigration Act 1971
by entering the UK in breach of a deportation order
the journey into the UK being a journey by water from France / Belgium / the Netherlands and
during the relevant period did an act
causing / creating a risk of death / serious personal injury
to another person

Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) If, on the trial of a person charged with an offence under section 24(E1A) in connection with the commission of an offence under section 24(A1), (B1), (D1) or (E1), the person is found not guilty of the offence charged, they may still be found guilty of an offence under subsection (A1), (B1), (D1) or (E1), as the case may be - see section 24(7).
(ii) This offence applies to conduct occurring both within and outside the United Kingdom - see section 24(6).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or fine.
Indictment : maximum 6 years imprisonment and / or fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 24(3) and section 28(1)
